title: Shortburst priming synthesis: bench draft for bursty short-turn chat
content:
Purpose
-------
Quick exploratory draft comparing priming/prefetch strategies for ultra-short chat turns (8–40 tokens) under bursty arrival patterns. Goal is to understand p50/p95 latency impact and $/1k-query delta for three practical approaches we could surface in the Console as knobs: streaming-only (baseline), compact-prefetch (client-side priming + server prewarm), and tiling/batch-squeeze (micro-tiling + background packing). Also a KV-hot variant (aggressive prefix caching) as a positive control.

High-level takeaway (TL;DR)
- For very short turns, compact-prefetch reduces p95 substantially vs streaming-only with modest cost increase.
- Tiling/batch-squeeze shows best $/1k for sustained high throughput but increases median latency on sporadic bursts.
- KV-hot gives the most consistent latency but needs cache hit shaping and TTL heuristics to avoid extra memory overhead.

Workload & test harness
- Workload: simulated chat with turn lengths sampled from empirical short-turn distribution (median 16 tokens, 90th 36). Inter-arrival: poisson with a configurable burst multiplier. We ran steady (1q/s), microburst (50q/s for 5s), and sustained-high (10q/s) scenarios.
- Model: open-variant-7B quantized (int8) on A100-40. Runtime config: 1-thread decode, streaming enabled where noted.
- Measurement captured client-observed latency (time from request send to first token) and server-side cost model (GPU-seconds + memory pressure amortized into $/1k queries using current infra rates).

Experiment matrix (labels used below)
- S: Streaming-only baseline (no server prewarm/prefetch).
- CP: Compact-prefetch — server receives a tiny priming request (50–100 tokens warmup) when session is detected; subsequent short turns benefit from warm KV/compiled kernels. Prefetch only on session start and once per TTL window.
- TS: Tiling/batch-squeeze — server opportunistically packs tiny turns into micro-tiles when concurrency > threshold; increases batch efficiency but may delay first token to assemble tiles.
- KV: Aggressive KV-hot — keep per-session prefix in hot memory across requests, immediate retrieval on next turn (higher mem use).

Annotated results (median numbers across runs; costs normalized to $/1k queries)
| Strategy | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | $/1k queries | Notes |
|----------|----------:|---------:|------------:|-------|
| S        | 72       | 360      | 0.140       | baseline streaming jitter on cold kernels and decode startup |
| CP       | 58       | 170      | 0.155       | warm kernels + KV prefix amortization, extra prewarm calls add cost |
| TS       | 85       | 190      | 0.090       | excellent amortized GPU cost but p50 penalty for low-concurrency bursts |
| KV       | 50       | 135      | 0.165       | best latency; memory & eviction complexity tradeoffs |

ASCII sparkline: p95 latency across minute-long microburst run (higher is worse)
S  : ███████████████████████████ (360ms)
CP : ████████████████ (170ms)
TS : ██████████████████ (190ms)
KV : ██████████████ (135ms)

Cost vs latency tradeoff summary
- TS minimizes $/1k for high sustained traffic (sustained throughput > 100 q/s) because packing raises token-utilization; however if traffic is dominated by intermittent microbursts, the median suffers.
- CP is a low-friction feature for developers: small upsell in cost (~10–12%) but large p95 wins for chat-like UX where tail matters. Console could expose TTL/threshold knobs (session priming TTL in seconds, prefetch token budget).

Operational observations
- Prefetch failure modes: failed prefetch increases p95 beyond S because the initial prewarm adds an extra RPC and if it times out we double-hit. We need tight timeouts and an opt-out fallback to streaming within 30–40ms.
- Tile assembly latency: in TS the packer waiting window (we used 6ms default) is critical. 0ms → no pack; >10ms → user-visible delay. Suggest default 4–6ms for mixed workloads.
- KV memory pressure: KV trials that keep per-session KV for >30s start to show 12–18% memory overhead on busy hosts. TTL heuristics tied to session activity are required.

Developer UX proposal (Console knobs)
- "Prefer latency" preset: enable CP with TTL=45s, prefetch token budget=128, fallback=stream-on-prefetch-failure.
- "Prefer cost" preset: enable TS with pack-window=5ms, pack-threshold=3, preempt-allowed=true.
- "KV-hot for VIP" (enterprise only): config toggle for pinned KV TTL + quota. Add advisory on memory footprint.

Open questions / TODOs
- Run CP+TS hybrid (prefetch + opportunistic packing) to see if we can get best of both worlds. Hypothesis: CP reduces p95; TS recoups cost on long tails. (Ticket: INFR-8972)
- Evaluate impact on long-turn sessions (>200 tokens) where prefetching might be wasteful. Need mixed-turn trace runs.
- Tune prefetch timeout policy: current 80ms seems high; test 30/50/80ms to measure penalty curve.

Bench artifacts & reproducibility notes
- Harness: bench-harness/shortburst in repo PR (see linked PR). Scripts are parameterized by burst multiplier and pack-window. Use docker image redwood/bench:shortburst-2029-08.
- Raw traces: s3://redwood-bench/shortburst/2029-08-12/ (private).

Suggested next steps before publishing as collateral
1) Run hybrid CP+TS experiment and produce one-page delta chart (p95 vs $/1k) for customer-facing collateral. 2) Add memory-cost estimator for KV mode to the Console UX so buyers can see expected host memory delta for given QPS. 3) Draft customer note: "How to choose Prefetch vs Pack: a short-turn playbook" with 3 one-line recipes.

Notes to reviewers
- This is a working draft intended for internal review by runtime and product. Expect numbers to shift with model variant and region pricing. I'm leaving some raw traces and script names in linked artifacts. Please annotate questions inline or drop notes in the Slack thread cited above.

Signed — Priya
